key_insight: Targeted repair can improve trustworthiness in distilled language models while largely preserving capabilities inherited from their teachers.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical alternative to re-distillation when the original distillation corpus is unavailable.
method: Use the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) to constrain changes during repair.
Estimate the required curvature from a surrogate proxy dataset.
Support preferred/dispreferred response pairs through an odds-ratio objective.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports trustworthiness improvements of up to 8% across different distilled models, with less than 1% degradation in perplexity, covering both pre-training and post-training models.
watch_item: Proxy-data selection may affect curvature estimates and repair quality; the abstract does not specify datasets, model sizes, or metric definitions.
paper_title: Repairing the Trustworthiness of Distilled Language Models
